processes.title: Lease record creation or modification
processes.purpose:
The purpose of this SOP is to explain the standard set of activities required to either create a new record or modify an existing record in the CoStar Real Estate Manager system. This includes different approaches for single record additions and updates, in addition to the potential for mass upload.

During the execution of this process, a user may determine a master data update is required in order to complete an addition or modification. This SOP advises of the necessary steps to take should this be the case. The process applies to all leases, both for AZ and Alexion, that meet the criteria of IFRS 16.

stages.title: Assess the lease and choose the entry route
stages.detail:
Start when a new lease accounting record is required or an existing record must be modified (renewal, termination, impairment or general modification). Check first whether an Accounting Issue Note (AIN) must be raised with GFR: issues with a financial impact above USD 10 million should be communicated to GFR, and unusual, complex or judgemental issues, or those with a profit impact above USD 20 million, need a full AIN.

Check whether the lease is short term (under 12 months) or low value (below USD 5,000). If so it is out of IFRS 16 scope: AstraZeneca leases and Alexion vehicle and equipment leases are expensed directly and not entered in CoStar, while Alexion property leases are marked Not Applicable in the CoStar accounting workflow.

Determine whether a mass upload should be requested. Mass upload is retained solely by the GFS Global Lease Team and may be requested when more than 30 lease records need creating or modifying, when an entity has over 300 active leases in an asset class, or for third-party vehicle lease data sent directly to the KL team. It should be a last resort; direct entry using CoStar productivity features such as record copying remains the most efficient route.

stages.title: Create the building and lease record in CoStar
stages.detail:
For real estate assets, add a Building in the CoStar Portfolio module with the country, building name (company code and lease reference), portfolio (AstraZeneca or Alexion), address, template and regional sub-group, then complete building details such as rentable area and building type.

Add a Lease to the building with the tenant legal name (company code), lease type (lessee or lessor position), begin and end dates per the contract, accounting type (AP for lessee or sublessee, AR for lessor or sublessor), currency and units of measure, then complete the lease abstract including the lease hierarchy (Region, Subregion, Country, and for Alexion the company code). The ERP field is populated automatically from the company code and directs the lease to either the SAP S/4HANA or the ECC (BlackLine) journal export.

For equipment assets, add an Equipment Lease from the Portfolio module with portfolio, supplier, legal entity, template, dates and currency, then complete the client lease ID, address, organisational hierarchy and ownership type.

stages.title: Enter the allocations that drive journal coding
stages.detail:
On the lease record open Allocations, edit and add an allocation, populating every segment before saving. AstraZeneca ECC parameters are Company Code, Cost Centre, Product Brand and Internal Order (using the Internal Order/WBS segment); AstraZeneca SAP S/4HANA parameters are Company Code, Cost Centre or WBS, and Product Brand, as internal orders are no longer used for S/4HANA markets. Alexion parameters are Accounting Company Code, Cost Centre, Payment Company Code and Cost Percent.

Enter the cost percent for each allocation line; most leases are allocated 100% to a single location, activity and banner, otherwise keep adding lines until the total reaches 100%. For Alexion the Payment Company Code is normally the same as the Accounting Company Code, which is the value that flows into the AJD file for posting in BlackLine.

stages.title: Enter expenses and generate the charge schedule
stages.detail:
On the Expenses page use Quick Add to create instalment and base rent charges. Choose fixed or rate entry, enter the amount, area, payment frequency, currency and start and end dates (defaulted from the lease abstract), and flag the charge as estimated, taxable or prorated where the conditions apply. The charge name is auto-populated from the account category; an initial expense is reflected as original term, and the name is changed for a modification.

Select the vendor (the single Filler RE Vendor for the AstraZeneca portfolio; for Alexion the actual vendor, added via the CoStar Company record if missing), enter the start amount and generate the charge. Review the resulting expense schedule for accuracy and add further charges as needed.

stages.title: Create the IFRS 16 accounting schedule
stages.detail:
On the Accounting page add a new accounting schedule. Select IFRS16 as the classification and amortisation profile, and the journal entry profile matching the asset type; profiles starting with S4 must be used for leases that have cut over to SAP S/4HANA and all other profiles for the remaining leases. Set the accounting term begin and end to the current commencement and expiration dates, accept the discount rate profile suggested by the system and adjust the payment timing if required.

Click Calculate Values, then save and close. For Alexion real estate, Global Real Estate / CBRE create the CoStar data for all leases except the accounting schedule, which the AZ Global Lease Team creates or modifies.

stages.title: Modify or remeasure an existing lease
stages.detail:
To modify charges, edit or delete the relevant charge on the Expense page (no overlapping dates), and for Alexion review payment dates and enter or exercise lease options in the abstract; these payment features do not apply to the AstraZeneca portfolio because CoStar does not process its payments.

A remeasurement is required for any change that revalues the right-of-use asset. For a renewal or data correction, first add or extend the fixed charges, then select Remeasure Renewal, enter the new accounting term begin and end, calculate values, verify the present value and adjustment amounts and save; a date range before an approved period produces a retroactive adjustment sent in the upcoming period. For an impairment, select Remeasure Impairment, enter the impairment date and a negative manual asset adjustment, calculate and save.

For a termination, select Remeasure Termination (normal expiry) or Full Termination (early termination), using the direct entry discount rate profile, the disposal journal entry profile for the asset type and a 0% annual rate so the gain or loss is calculated. If the effective date falls in an exported period, move the workflow status to Open for Preparation and ask the Global Lease Accounting Team to unexport and unapprove the affected journals before remeasuring. After any remeasurement, review the schedule and update the accounting workflow status.

stages.title: Submit the lease record for approval
stages.detail:
Submit the record by changing its workflow status from Open for Preparation to Prepared in CoStar. It then reaches the queue of the relevant approvers for the country or entity: the Global Lease Team as a technical-only activity, or the Embedded Finance or Middle Office controllers where the SOX/FCF controls require local approval. For Alexion, Controllership approves real estate and BP70 equipment leases while the Global Lease Team approves vehicle leases as low-value impact.

Check whether errors exist. If they do, repeat the lease entry task until every error is corrected in the system; if not, the record proceeds to the Approve and review a lease accounting record process.

processes.title: Lease record review and approval
processes.purpose:
The purpose of this SOP is to explain the activities required to approve and review a newly created or modified lease record, to ensure the record is accurate, complete and valid from an accounting perspective, before it is included in the period end activity that generates the relevant IFRS 16 general ledger accounting entries.

The executor of an approval will depend on a country's classification in the control environment. The GFS Global Lease Team will carry out this activity as a technical step for the majority of entities. However, the largest entities (top 80% liabilities value in USD) will require a local approval.

stages.title: Approve individual records for SOX and top-80% entities
stages.detail:
Check whether the record belongs to a SOX entity or one of the top 80% of entities by USD liability value. If so, the approver navigates to the lease reference, opens Accounting, confirms the workflow status is Prepared, and reviews accuracy and completeness against the description for which the lease was opened for preparation.

Once reviewed, insert a comment specific to the change type (for example approved for addition, disposal or modification), change the status from Prepared to Approved and save. The review of the CoStar Accounting Summary report that confirms leases are complete and at Approved or Reviewed status is SOX and FCF control CPX015-01, and CoStar enforces segregation of duties in the approval workflow under control CPX016-01.

stages.detail:
In the Accounting module open Batch Change Workflow and filter by portfolio, IFRS 16 classification, workflow status Prepared and the relevant hierarchy and country. Extract the roll-forward report (see Execute lease accounting reporting) to review accuracy and completeness of the filtered leases.

Select the leases to approve, click Update Leases, choose the new status and enter a comment stating the number and type of changes, then process the changes. The process log can be exported to Excel. If a record is not successfully approved because it is inaccurate or incomplete, it returns to the Create or modify a lease accounting record process for correction.

processes.title: Lease accounting reporting
processes.purpose: The purpose of this SOP is to explain the standard set of activities required to generate a report from CoStar Real Estate Manager. This could be one of the standard, pre-configured reports, or a user created report, depending on the underlying requirement. All users have full access to the CoStar reporting module and are expected to self-serve their own reporting demands.
processes.cadence: This process can be ad hoc as required or executed regularly as part of a period end close process such as schedule/disclosure submissions and balance sheet reconciliation.

stages.title: Document the report request
stages.detail: Users without CoStar access request a lease accounting report from a licensed CoStar user via AZNextgen or Outlook. The CoStar user checks whether a suitable report already exists: if it does, it is executed with the required parameters; if not, a report is created or modified.

stages.title: Create or modify an ad hoc report
stages.detail:
In the Reports module click Create Report, name it, choose Excel or PDF format and select a data set such as Lease Summary, GL Event Summary, Lease Allocations or Lease Accounting. Decide whether to return active, archived or both records, add the required fields and set criteria on the data (for example commencement date after today). Users with access to both portfolios must filter on the relevant portfolio.

Run the report, save it if it will be reused and optionally add it to Favourites. To modify an existing report, open it via the ellipsis, edit the selected fields and save.

stages.description:

Users with access to both portfolios must filter on the relevant portfolio.

Run the report, save it if it will be reused and optionally add it to Favourites. To modify an existing report, open it via the ellipsis, edit the selected fields and save.

stages.title: Share or schedule the report
stages.detail: Right-click the report name and choose Share to assign rights to a user or group. To receive the report periodically, choose Schedule and specify the schedule name, frequency, begin and end dates and the email delivery list, which can include CoStar and non-CoStar users, then save.

stages.title: Test and reconcile the report
stages.detail: Locate the saved or modified report in the Reports module and check that its output is accurate and complete. If it is, execute it with the required parameters; if not, return to create or modify the report.

stages.title: Reverse the journal status of a single lease
stages.detail:
Once a lease journal is approved and exported, its JE status moves from Scheduled to Approved to Exported and it no longer appears in the approve or export screens, preventing reprocessing. To modify an accounting schedule after export, open the lease Accounting page, click the Exported status for the period, review the entry, select Unexport and then Unapprove, and confirm the status is back to Scheduled before making changes.

After the changes, reprocess the period through Journal Entries to Approve and the relevant export. Whenever an unexport or unapprove is performed in CoStar, a reversal journal must be prepared manually and posted in BlackLine under the normal BlackLine journal policy.

After the changes, reprocess the period through Journal Entries to Approve and the relevant export. Whenever an unexport or unapprove is performed in CoStar, a reversal journal must be prepared manually and posted in BlackLine under the normal BlackLine journal policy.

stages.detail:

CoStar generates an Excel file.

In the file set the Action column for each row (unapprove or skip for Approved; unexport, unexport and unapprove, or skip for Exported), save it and upload it via Upload Offline Template; processing can take up to 15 minutes.

processes.title: Depreciation calculation and recording
processes.purpose:
This Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) sets out the mandatory activities to calculate and record depreciation expenses. This process covers the depreciation activities for the month, as well as the steps required when any errors or variances are identified while performing the depreciation run. The process for this activity also includes a mid-month test run for depreciation, to reduce the likelihood of error during the month end calculation.

The intangible assets SOP directs the monthly amortisation of intangible assets to this same procedure: all intangible asset posting requests (acquisition, retirement, disposal and impairment) are sent to GFS Back Office R2R as pre-closing activities and the amortisation is executed with the depreciation run.

stages.title: Execute the mid-month depreciation test run
stages.detail:
Before month-end close, run the depreciation posting programme (AFAB) in test mode for the company code, current fiscal year and posting period with List Assets ticked, in all regions except NAM, which has no mid-month scheduled job. Run in the foreground where the asset count is low (limited to around 1,000 assets) or in the background where it is high, checking the finished job and its spool via Own Jobs. A successful run ends with TESTRUN completed successfully; failures are typically posting to a month already posted or to a subsequent month before the current period.

Export the results to Excel and load them into the AFAB tab of the FA Movement and Analysis Template (saving last month's file as the current month file and moving the prior data to the AFAB last month tab). The workbook looks up each asset's prior month depreciation and calculates the difference; variances above USD 1 million by account determination or above 5% must be explained by the preparer.

# PURPOSE

This Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) sets out the mandatory activities to calculate and record Depreciation expenses. This process covers the depreciation activities for the month, as well as the steps required when any errors or variances are identified while performing the depreciation run. The process for this activity also includes a mid-month test run for depreciation, to reduce the likelihood of error during the month end calculation.

## Frequency

Monthly, as specified in the Global Close Calendar.

## Controls

The table below contains a summary of the Controls in the related process map:

|  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|
| Control Id / Name | Control Type | Control Objective | Control Owner |
| CPX011 | SOX | What controls exist to ensure that monthly depreciation charges are calculated accurately? | GFS Back Office R2R |

Note: Please note: The control objective defines the risk that needs to be addressed by the control. For the definition and for detailed information on the control operated for your unit, please refer to [FCAS](http://seskwfcswbp01.emea.astrazeneca.net/) for your unit.

## Process Detail

Task # | TASK NAME
8.3.3.6.1 | Execute Initial Depreciation mid-month (Test Run)
8.3.3.6.2 | Investigate error
8.3.3.6.3 | Assist with Error Resolution

8.3.3.6.5 | Complete all asset postings
8.3.3.6.6 | Execute Depreciation at month end (test run)
8.3.3.6.7 | Contact IT Help Desk & Raise Ticket
8.3.3.6.8 | Resolve Error
8.3.3.6.9 | Perform variance analysis against prior month depreciation
8.3.3.6.10 | Investigate Variance
8.3.3.6.11 | Provide assistance with Variance Explanation
8.3.3.6.12 | Coordinate to update Fixed Assets Master Data
8.3.3.6.13 | Include variance analysis in month-end reconciliation
8.3.3.6.14 | Execute Depreciation (Production)

processes.title: Project closure and capitalisation
processes.purpose:
This Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) sets out the mandatory activities for the closure and capitalisation of a project. Open capital projects are monitored monthly, the Business confirms which projects are ready to close, asset shells are created, project costs are settled from the WBSE to the asset under construction and then to the final assets, open commitments are cleared and the project status is set to closed (or released again if further cost must be booked).

The settlement of assets under construction to final assets is subject to SOX control CPX005B / CPX005BC, which ensures that only valid, completed capital projects are included in the fixed assets register and that amounts are recorded completely and accurately.

stages.title: Generate the open capital projects report
stages.detail:
Each month extract open projects with actual cost and budget from the project system (CN41N, PS info profile, company code and project mask E* plus any older codes) into the Data ALL tab of the Open Capital Project Report. Extract the AUC balances from the asset history sheet (AR02 or S_ALR_87011990) for the AUC asset classes, current month end, depreciation area 20 and the WBSE sort variant with layout /MEO, and list the AUC assets with their WBSE reference (S_ALR_87012058).

Match AUC balances to project definitions in Excel with lookups and a pivot, confirm the AUC balances tie to AR02, and verify the sub-ledger AUC balance against the general ledger (F.01, chart of accounts SCOA, AUC GL accounts); any mismatch is explained by manual postings to AUC GL 12100901 and supported in the Manual Posting tab. The report also supports CAPEX 3 reporting of cumulative authorised budget. Save the report as values and share it with GFS Middle Office and the project managers. Metric FA_4.3.3 tracks the ageing of open projects since their last transaction.

processes.purpose:
This Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) sets out the mandatory activities for the process relating to the creation of a fixed asset code for fixed asset addition(s) either through the direct purchase of an asset(s) or through capitalisation of capital projects. Business needs to identify the type of fixed asset addition being processed.

For non-commercial entities, any asset addition will need to go through Project System, starting with a project creation under the Review and approve capital projects process. Project System tracks capital expenditure by E-code WBSE for all non-commercial units and settles it into an Asset Under Construction (AUC); on project completion or partial completion the asset is put into use through the Close and Capitalise Projects process. Transfers between legal entities are retired in the billing entity, invoiced through a Non-Trade Invoice and received in the receiving entity through a standard NTI project.

# PURPOSE

This Standard Operating Procedure (SOP), sets out the mandatory activities for the process relating to the creation of a fixed asset code for fixed asset addition(s) either through the direct purchase of an asset(s) or through capitalisation of capital projects.

Business needs to identify the type of fixed asset addition being processed.

For Non-Commercial Entities, any asset additions (“Direct addition of a fixed asset”) will need to go through Project System. The process will need to start with a Project Creation, please proceed to **8.4.1.3 Review and approve capital projects** process map for additional details.

Project System is used to track capital expenditure by E-code WBSE for all non-commercial units and settled into Asset Under Construction (AUC). Upon project completion or partial completion, asset will be put into use following asset additions via the AUC process. Please refer to process **8.4.2.4 Close and Capitalise Projects** process map for additional details.

If addition type is “Transfer between legal entities” then the following process needs to be followed:

The process for the billing entity (the entity sending the asset to the receiving entity) is to first retire the asset through the process **8.3.3.10 Process and Record Fixed Asset Retirements**.

The billing / sending entity will then issue a Non-Trade Invoice (NTI) to the receiving entity through the process **8.3.2.12 Post Intercompany Non-Trade Transactions** (Please see the process map for additional details).

On the other hand, the receiving entity will need to create the transferred asset using the Project System module. A standard project will will be used for the purpose of receiving the cost from the billing entity. The standard of naming of this NTI project is as follows:

E.AA \, 2nd level \, next level \ e.g. E.AA0010.99.01 refers to an NTI-based asset transfer project for UK (company code 0010), for a tangible asset (next level posting key of 01). This project needs to be created just once and maintained in “TECO” status until an asset transfer needs to be initiated.

In case the receiving entity’s project is at system status “Closed” or “TECO”, the receiving entity will need to request for the project status update by sending E-Code WBSE Maintenance Form to GFS Back Office DMT team to set system status to “Released”. Please refer to activity **4.7.17 Release Project** under process **8.4.2.4 Close and Capitalise Projects for additional details.**

Upon receiving the NTI, the invoice will need to be posted into standard Capital Expenditure GL 99100010 with the WBSE. **Note** that for NAM and UK, GL 70770150 is currently used as shown in the sample given below. processes.title: Fixed asset impairments
processes.purpose:
The process of asset impairment is required to accurately reflect the recoverable value of assets in the fixed asset register. This applies to both tangible and intangible assets.

The carrying values of non-financial assets should be reviewed at least annually to determine whether there is any indication of impairment due to external and internal factors. This process covers the processing and recording of fixed asset impairments, whether value based (posted as unplanned depreciation), time based (a change of useful life) or, where the sub-ledger cannot be updated in time, through a one-time financial accounting journal or a provision.

stages.title: Perform the tangible and intangible asset review
stages.detail: Review the carrying values of non-financial assets at least annually, and whenever a business trigger event may affect carrying value or useful life, by comparing the balance sheet carrying value with the recoverable amount for the assets listed in the Group Accounting Manual section D1. This review is SOX control CPX013 (UK and Sweden hubs continue to operate CPX010). Share the outcome with the Business: an impairment leads to the list of assets for impairment, a provision to the provision journal, and no action ends the process.

stages.title: Prepare the impairment list and accounting treatment
stages.detail:
Using the asset review report, list the assets subject to impairment and determine the treatment, consulting GFR if needed. For a value-related impairment complete the Assets Impairment Template with the asset number, description, acquisition date and value and NBV, taken from the asset explorer (AW01N, posted values and master data) for a single asset or the asset balances report (S_ALR_87011963, depreciation area 01) for several; if the posting date is in a later month, reduce the NBV by the planned depreciation up to the preceding period.

For a time-related impairment that shortens useful life, complete the Assets Master Data Maintenance Template with the current useful life read from the depreciation areas (AS03) and the agreed reason; local GAAP changes must be confirmed by the country finance controller.

If the treatment or the template does not agree with the asset register, advise the Business to amend the request; if approved, the Business raises the impairment request.

The Business submits a major strategic impairment request by email to GFS Back Office R2R, whose fixed assets team lead assesses case by case, considering the volume of assets, whether it can be completed in the sub-ledger by month-end close. If the month's depreciation is already posted, unplanned depreciation can only be posted in the next period, so a manual journal is posted for the current period and reversed the following month.

processes.title: Fixed asset retirements
processes.purpose:
This Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) sets out the mandatory activities for processing and recording fixed asset retirements.

Fixed assets can be retired either by transfer (within a legal entity or between legal entities), or through a system-based retirement (with or without an invoice). To initiate the asset retirement process, upon request from the Business, Embedded Finance / GFS Middle Office will complete the Assets Retirement Request Template and obtain approval from the appropriate approver as per the Global Delegation of Authority (DOA). Once approved, the request is routed to GFS Back Office DMT for transfers within the same legal entity, or to GFS Back Office R2R for all other types of retirement, who validate the request details against the DOA and SAP (approver, cost centre, net book value) and inform the Business by email once complete.

For a transfer within a legal entity without asset class change, complete the Assets Master Data Maintenance template with the recipient cost centre and maintenance type CHANGE (no DOA approval needed, team lead approval only). For a transfer within a legal entity with asset class change, complete the Assets Transfer Request Template, indicating whether receiver asset numbers already exist and supplying the instance-specific fields for the UK, Sweden or NAM.

For a transfer to another legal entity, or a retirement with or without invoice, complete the Assets Retirement Request Template including the NBV, checked in SAP by displaying the asset (AS03, posted values) or the asset balances report (S_ALR_87011963, depreciation area 01) for several assets, and verifying the asset number, description, capitalisation date and acquisition value. The template must be authorised by an approver with DOA activity 2003 (Capital Expenditure and Asset Disposal).

For a transfer within a legal entity with asset class change, complete the Assets Transfer Request Template, indicating whether receiver asset numbers already exist and supplying the instance-specific fields for the UK, Sweden or NAM.

stages.detail:
For regulatory reasons the financial transfer is processed when the physical transfer occurs. The selling entity issues an NTI to the receiving entity through the Post Intercompany Non-Trade Transactions process and retires the asset to the gain or loss account, with GFS Back Office C2C or P2P posting the customer or vendor side during NTI posting; the receiving entity posts the NTI to a project and capitalises through the Fixed Asset Additions process.

This validation is FCF control CPX008. Obtain the FA team lead's approval, post the retirement (ABAVN) with the asset or list of assets, dates, retirement effective date, text, period, document type AA and reference, simulate and post, then verify the deactivation date and blank NBV (AS03) and the document (FB03), and email the requester.

stages.description:
For regulatory reasons the financial transfer is processed when the physical transfer occurs. The selling entity issues an NTI to the receiving entity through the Post Intercompany Non-Trade Transactions process and retires the asset to the gain or loss account, with GFS Back Office C2C or P2P posting the customer or vendor side during NTI posting; the receiving entity posts the NTI to a project and capitalises through the Fixed Asset Additions process.

Retrieve the Assets Retirement Request Template, verify in the Global DOA portal (activity code 2003) that the email approver is authorised for the amount, and validate the asset in SAP (AS03 or S_ALR_87011963: capitalisation date, Deactivated On blank, cost centre, class, description and NBV), querying discrepancies to the requester. This validation is FCF control CPX008. Obtain the FA team lead's approval, post the retirement (ABAVN) with the asset or list of assets, dates, retirement effective date, text, period, document type AA and reference, simulate and post, then verify the deactivation date and blank NBV (AS03) and the document (FB03), and email the requester.

stages.title: Retire the asset by scrapping or with sales proceeds
stages.detail:
Under control CPX008, retire a scrapped asset (ABAVN) for the company code and asset or list of assets, with the processing dates, the retirement effective date as asset value date, Asset Retirement text, posting period, document type AA and reference; enter the partial amount or percentage on the Partial Retirement tab where the template requests a partial retirement, simulate to review the entries and post. Verify the deactivation date and blank NBV (AS03) and the document (FB03).

For a non-invoice retirement with sales proceeds, post through the asset retirement with revenue transaction (F-92), debiting (posting key 40) the GL provided by the requester or the bank clearing account confirmed with GFS Back Office C2C Cash and Banking; where proceeds are deducted from an employee's salary account use that GL or employee code, and for a vendor deduction use posting key 21 against the vendor code. Notify the requester on completion.

Notify the requester on completion.

stages.detail: For mass retirements, run the asset balances report (S_ALR_87011990) for the company code and assets, create a worklist from the list with the task Retirement without Revenue, posting and document dates, transaction type 200 and the retirement effective date, and note the worklist number. # PURPOSE

This Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) sets out the mandatory activities for processing and recording fixed asset retirements.

Fixed assets can be retired either by transfer (within a legal entity or between legal entities), or through a system-based retirement (with or without an invoice). To initiate the asset retirement process, upon request from the Business, Embedded Finance / GFS Middle Office will complete the Assets Retirement Request Template and obtain approval from the appropriate approver as per the Global Delegation of Authority (DOA).

Once approved, the Assets Master Data Maintenance Template will either be routed to GFS Back Office DMT for transfers within the same legal entities, or Assets Retirement Request Template and Assets Transfer Request Template to GFS Back Office R2R for all other types of retirement. GFS Back Office DMT and GFS Back Office R2R will access the template for details with regard to the retirement.

GFS Back Office R2R will then perform validation of the request details and check the supporting documents against DOA and SAP. Examples of items to check are the approver, the cost centre and the net book value of the asset. Once the process is completed, GFS Back Office DMT and GFS Back Office R2R will inform the Business via Email.

## Frequency

This process happens on an ad-hoc basis, as per request from the Business.

## Controls

The table below contains a summary of the control(s) for the process this operating procedure relates to:

|  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|
| Control Id / Name | Control Type | Control Objective | Control Owner |
| CPX008 | FCF | What controls exist to ensure that capital disposals are valid? | GFS Back Office R2R |

Please note: The control objective defines the risk that needs to be addressed by the control. For the definition and for detailed information on the control operated for your unit, please refer to [FCAS](http://seskwfcswbp01.emea.astrazeneca.net/) for your unit.

8.3.3.10.3 | Submit or amend request to transfer, decommission or sell asset. Obtain approvals as per DOA
8.3.3.10.4 | Update fixed asset master data
8.3.3.10.5 | Transfer the asset within legal entity
8.3.3.10.6 | Execute transactions to retire asset
8.3.3.10.7 | Retire partial or entire asset from Fixed Assets Register
8.3.3.10.8 | Retire entire asset for an invoice sale
8.3.3.10.9 | Create and transmit customer invoice
8.3.3.10.10 | Receive confirmation that asset has been retired

Review and validate salary, time, material and T&E expenses for completeness, accuracy and propriety, then send a review request to the project managers, who confirm all costs posted are valid; costs not directly associated with the project must not be posted to it, and capital project expenses are capitalised monthly and when the asset is ready for service. stages.detail:
Before the fixed asset module closes each month, settle capital project WBSE costs to the corresponding AUC via the settlement rules; this control point zeroes costs on all capital projects at month end (not applicable to Brazil pending SAP configuration; NAM runs a daily settlement job at 23:00 US time plus manual month-end settlement). Run the individual settlement (CJ88) in test mode for the WBSE, review the detail list and resolve red errors where the settlement exceeds the AUC balance (yellow warnings for remaining AUC balances need no action), then run the actual settlement.

For mass settlement run CJ8G for the controlling area with the regional variant, period, automatic processing, test run, detail list and check transaction data, in background where needed, checking the job (SMX) and fixing settlement rule errors (CJ02: AUC as receiver, 100%, type FUL, current period) before the final run. Confirm the settlement moved costs from the WBSE to AUC by checking 99101090 and 99100010 net to zero (CJI3 or F.01), that the AUC GL received the posting (FBL3N) and that the WBSE actual costs are zero at month end.

This Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) sets out the mandatory activities for the capital project approval process.

Capital projects are reviewed and approved through the CAS system. As an output of the process, if a capital project is approved, the Embedded Finance / GFS Middle Office team will submit a request to GFS Back Office DMT to create a project account code. In other cases, the project could be deferred until the following year or terminated if it is no longer required.

processes.purpose:
This Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) sets out the mandatory activities for tracking physical fixed assets. Physical fixed assets require regular tracking to ensure that the assets recorded in the system are consistent with the physical assets on site.

This process covers the tracking of fixed assets, including performing physical inventory checks. The process is linked with processing retirements and impairments: following completion of asset verification, the Business will determine if there are asset retirements and impairments that must be performed. The periodic confirmation of the existence of fixed assets is SOX control CPX010.
processes.cadence: The control for fixed asset verification should be performed annually and all fixed assets (as per the Capital and Fixed Asset Standard) should be verified once in three years.

stages.title: Generate the fixed asset list for the review scope
stages.detail:
All entities must physically verify assets with an NBV above a locally defined threshold at least once every three years; verification frequency varies by region and market (annual, two-yearly or three-yearly, with some LATAM markets exempt). For the hubs the exercise is triggered after the June month-end close and for other markets in September.

Run the asset history sheet (AR02 or S_ALR_87011990) for the company code and report date, the regional depreciation area, excluding AUC and intangible classes, with the sort variant that shows cost centre and location, layout Select CPX010, and export it to Excel. Allocate the listing by location, cost centre and responsible person per the country's control description and email the in-scope tangible assets to each point of contact; for example the UK and Sweden verify assets representing at least 85% of net book value plus manually recorded items annually, and NAM works a three-year plan by NBV band.
